headline: Curated databases pair molecular records with 3D structures and binding or probing data
label: Structure Linked Curated Biological Databases
summary: Four late-2026 releases link structural models to binding, probing, and antiviral evidence across toxins, RNA, and plant viruses.
synthesis: The common thread is curation that anchors heterogeneous molecular measurements to structural models. ToxINsight links 2,078 snake venom toxin entries to 2,540 3D structures, with alignment and ligand-binding analysis. ARIEL pairs manually curated experimental RNA-ligand Kd values with 278 nonredundant 3D complexes. Ribocentre-FoldBridge connects RNA chemical probing profiles to X-ray crystallographic and cryo-EM models. PlantVirDisConDB integrates plant virus sequences with hosts, diseases, targets, and antiviral assay data, and adds AI-assisted molecule-virus activity prioritization. The new element is structure-anchored, queryable evidence spanning toxins, RNA, and plant viruses. AI assistance is described explicitly only for PlantVirDisConDB's prioritization; the provided summaries do not describe LLM-based access in any item. The dominant thread is integrative curation rather than a shared data type, since the resources differ in target molecule and assay format.
